title: dlnmpy: distributed lag non-linear models in Python
description:
A Python port of the R package dlnm by Antonio Gasparrini and Ben Armstrong, written from the published methodology and the R source, and validated numerically against R.

Distributed lag non-linear models (DLNMs) are the standard method for exposure-lag-response associations in environmental epidemiology, above all for temperature and mortality. This package makes the method usable from Python, together with the surrounding workflow that R leaves to loose scripts: the minimum mortality temperature, attributable fractions, two-stage designs and the standard figures.

Validation. Every expected value in the test suite is generated by an R script committed in the repository. Six published analyses by the original authors are reproduced end to end, matching their published headline numbers: Gasparrini et al. 2015 (The Lancet), Gasparrini & Armstrong 2013 (BMC Medical Research Methodology), Gasparrini & Leone 2014 (attributable risk), Gasparrini 2014 (Statistics in Medicine), Vicedo-Cabrera, Sera & Gasparrini 2019 (Epidemiology), and Gasparrini et al. 2017 (Biometrics).

Not affiliated with the authors of dlnm. The method is theirs; this package makes it usable from Python.
